newsitem.title: UK: Copper, aluminium post strong finish on LME.
newsitem.headline: Copper, aluminium post strong finish on LME.

text.p: Copper finished substantially firmer on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Friday, hanging on to most of the gains from a brisk early rally.
Technical buying and aggressive short covering took copper to fresh 8-1/2 month highs despite an unexpected stocks increase of 1,875 tonnes.
It was at $2,366 per tonne at the afternoon kerb close, off the day's $2,375 high but nevertheless up $38 from Thursday's finish.
The red metal's break above the $2,350 area -- an important point from a downtrend dating back to August 1995 -- pointed to continued gains, some analysts said.
"Copper has made a strong close and it looks like prices will be targetting the $2,400 psychological level," said analyst Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff.
Expectations that Chinese demand was on the rise in the near term was seen leading to tightening in the market in future, piquing market interest, analysts said.
Cash to threes backwardation was slightly narrower at $73/$78.
Aluminium was also notably firmer after breaching resistance around $1,615, thereby triggering buy-stops.
A drawdown of 2,400 tonnes in LME stocks, along with stronger copper, helped aluminium.
It ended the kerb at the day's highs of $1,631, which was $24 firmer than on Thursday.
"Aluminium has also had a good close for the week, and proved it had good underlying support. Good buying has been exposed," Squires said.
It was now targetting the $1,551 and then $1,700 resistance areas, Squires said.
The other base metals exhibited less buoyancy.
Nickel finished off its highs, drifting below the $7,900 level to close just $25 firmer at $7,875.
Lead wound up little changed at $669, just $2 firmer, despite a drawdown of 1,050 tonnes.
Tin and zinc ended slightly lower after bids to follow copper higher failed amid lack of interest and follow through buying.
Tin was last at $5,980, down $40, while zinc was off $5 at $1,211.
Alloy was last a firmer $1,550, versus $1,532/35.
